title_en: The Signs of the Hour, Part Two
body_ar: ومن لم يؤمن إلا بعد مشاهدة الأشراط الكبرى فإيمانه لا يغني عنه من الله شيئا لأنه مثل إيمان الغرق بعد أن غرق، كحال فرعون عندما قال: {آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنوا إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين}، أما الأشراط الصغرى فقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعضها في سؤال جبريل حين سأله فقال: فأخبرني عن أماراتها قال: أن تلد الأمة ربتها وفي رواية ربها وأن ترى الحفاة العراة العالة رعاء الشاء يتطاولون في البنيان، فهنا بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أشراط الساعة الصغرى أن تلد الأمة ربتها وفي رواية أن تلد الأمة ربها،
body_en:
Whoever does not believe until after he has seen the major signs — his faith will avail him nothing with God, because it is like the faith of a drowning man after he has already drowned, as was the case with Pharaoh when he said: {I believe that there is no god but the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am one of those who submit.} (Sūrat Yūnus 10:90).

As for the minor signs, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out some of them in Gabriel's questioning, when he asked him and said: 'Then tell me about its marks.' He said: 'That the bondwoman will give birth to her mistress' — and in another narration, 'to her master' — 'and that you will see the barefoot, the naked, the destitute herdsmen of sheep competing with one another in raising tall buildings.' So here the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out, among the minor signs of the Hour, that the bondwoman will give birth to her mistress — and in another narration, that the bondwoman will give birth to her master,

flags.arabic: أن تلد الأمة ربتها وفي رواية ربها
flags.context: The minor signs of the Hour, quoted from the hadith of Gabriel.
options: that the bondwoman will give birth to her mistress / to her master
that the slave-girl will give birth to her mistress / to her master
that the handmaid will bear her own mistress / her own master
flags.note: الأمة here is the female slave (al-amah), not the community (al-ummah) discussed in article 499; the two are written identically without vowels and an English reader must not be allowed to confuse them. The Sheikh deliberately reports both transmitted readings, ربتها (her mistress) and ربها (her master), and interprets neither; no interpretation has been added.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
The source spells بنوا إسرائيل for بنو إسرائيل in the Qur'anic quotation; this is orthographic only and does not affect the sense.
إيمان الغرق has been read as إيمان الغَرِق, 'the faith of the drowning man', which the following clause بعد أن غرق confirms.
The page begins mid-argument — it continues article 499 — and so carries no opening invocation.
